articles.title: A Tiny Robot That Swims With Living Muscle
articles.summary: MIT scientists built a gum-sized robot that swims using living muscle cells. The cells squeeze when light shines on them, letting the robot steer through water — and one day it may work in fragile places too delicate for ordinary machines.

articles.title: Halley's Comet Leaves a Trail of Shooting Stars
articles.summary: Earth is passing through dust left behind by Halley's Comet, making the Orionid meteor shower. A photographer in Georgia captured three bright meteors near Orion, and the shower stays active until Nov. 7.

articles.title: A $10 Chip That Could Put a Lab on Your Wrist
articles.summary: Cambridge researchers built a spectrometer that costs about $10 and is only a few centimeters wide. It identified materials perfectly in tests and even measured blood sugar without needles, though it needs much more testing before medical use.
